newsitem.title: USA: UAL JULY PASSENGER LOAD FACTOR OFF.
newsitem.headline: UAL JULY PASSENGER LOAD FACTOR OFF.

text.p: UAL Corp said Thursday the July passenger load factor for its United Airlines dropped to 75.1 percent from 75.6 percent a year ago.

North American load factor rose in July to 75.9 percent from 75.2 percent a year ago, and Latin American load factor increased to 72.5 percent from 69.6 percent. Atlantic load factor went up to 82.9 percent from 82.4 percent.
Pacific load factor, however, fell 5.4 percentage points to 69.7 percent from 75.1 percent.

"We are pleased to report gains in passenger load factors for our domestic, Latin American and Atlantic markets," John Edwardson, president, said in a statement. "Also noteworthy was a surge of 25.8 percent in cargo ton miles which continues an ongoing favorable trend."
UAL said cargo ton miles in July rose to 243.3 million from 193.4 million.

For the month, total revenue passenger miles for scheduled service rose 3.4 percent to 11.21 billion, including a 2.8 percent gain in North America to 7.0 billion. Atlantic revenues passenger miles rose 23.3 percent to 1.33 billion, while Pacific miles fell 3.2 percent to 2.37 billion.

Total available seat miles for July rose 4.1 percent to 14.94 billion from 14.35 billion a year ago. That included a two percent rise in North America to 9.24 billion and a 22.5 percent rise in the Atlantic market to 1.61 billion.

Year-to-date, total passenger load factor was up 0.2 percentage points to 71.8 percent. Total revenues passenger miles rose 4.1 percent to 69.74 billion and total available seat miles gained 3.9 percent to 97.15 billion.
